title: Server: add a short-TTL cache for Clerk getUser and use it in HTTP + socket auth
description:
Today every authenticated HTTP request (`authenticateToken` / `attachOptionalUser`, server/utils/auth.js:39 and :66) and every Socket.IO handshake (`socketAuthMiddleware`, server/index.js ~line 300) calls `clerkClient.users.getUser(userId)` — a network round trip to Clerk per request, adding latency and counting against Clerk's backend API rate limits.

In server/utils/auth.js: add `getClerkUserCached(userId)` backed by `lru-cache` (already a dependency, used in middleware/rateLimit.js) with `ttl: 30_000` and a bounded `max` (e.g. 5000). Cache the in-flight Promise so concurrent requests for the same user share one Clerk call; on rejection, delete the entry so failures are never cached (callers keep their existing fallback-to-`mapAuthenticatedUser(userId, null)` behaviour unchanged). Add `invalidateClerkUser(userId)` and `clearClerkUserCache()` (for tests). Replace both `clerkClient.users.getUser(userId)` calls with `getClerkUserCached(userId)`. Export the three new functions alongside the existing exports.

In server/index.js `socketAuthMiddleware`: replace `clerkClient.users.getUser(socket.userId)` with `getClerkUserCached(socket.userId)` from './utils/auth'. The fail-closed JWT check (`verifyToken`) must stay exactly as-is — only the ban lookup is cached (server-invariants: never fail-open a socket JWT check).

In server/routes/admin.js: call `invalidateClerkUser(targetId)` right after the successful `updateUserMetadata` in the ban handler (~line 65) and `invalidateClerkUser(req.params.id)` after the unban handler (~line 82), so a ban takes effect immediately on this instance. On other instances (if ever scaled out) the 30s TTL bounds staleness — acceptable and worth noting in a comment. Do not change isAdmin resolution logic (server-invariants: isAdmin comes from Clerk metadata or ADMIN_USER_IDS).

title: Server tests: cover the Clerk user cache and keep socket auth test mocks in sync
description:
server/tests/socketAuthMiddleware.test.js fully mocks '../utils/auth' with only `clerkClient.users.getUser`; after step 1 index.js calls `getClerkUserCached`, so add `getClerkUserCached: (...a) => mockGetUser(...a)` to that mock (keep existing assertions on mockGetUser working).

New server/tests/clerkUserCache.test.js (pure unit test, no DB): mock '@clerk/backend' `createClerkClient` to return a client whose `users.getUser` is a jest.fn, require '../utils/auth', `clearClerkUserCache()` in beforeEach. Cases: (a) two sequential calls for the same id -> getUser called once; (b) two concurrent calls -> called once; (c) a rejected call is not cached — next call retries; (d) `invalidateClerkUser(id)` forces a refetch; (e) different ids are cached separately. Use jest fake timers or advance Date to verify TTL expiry triggers a refetch.

Gate: `cd server && PORT=3099 npx jest tests/clerkUserCache.test.js tests/socketAuthMiddleware.test.js tests/adminActions.test.js tests/authUnauthenticated401.test.js --runInBand --detectOpenHandles --forceExit`.

Added during execution: server/tests/adminActions.test.js also fully mocks '../utils/auth', so admin.js's new `invalidateClerkUser` import was undefined there; added it to that mock and asserted ban/unban call it.
